shortDescription: By Emily Ou YongJapanese rubber futures edged higher on Wednesday, supported by tight supply as tapping in China nears an end, although lower oil prices and a slide in Tokyo equities capped gains.($1 = 159.2400 yen)($1 = 6.6640 Chinese yuan)

children: Japanese rubber futures edged higher on Wednesday, supported by tight supply as tapping in China nears an end, although lower oil prices and a slide in Tokyo equities capped gains.
The Osaka Exchange (OSE) rubber contract for May delivery
was up 1.1 yen, or 0.26%, at 422.9 yen ($2.66) per kg as of 0225 GMT
The rubber contract on the Shanghai Futures Exchange (SHFE) for January delivery
rose 60 yuan, or 0.33%, to 18,475 yuan ($2,772.36) per metric ton
The most active January butadiene rubber contract on the SHFE (SHBRv1) gained 140 yuan, or 0.95%, to 14,850 yuan per metric ton

Cumulative year-on-year declines in output in major producing regions continue to support prices, and raw material prices remain resilient as tapping in China's production areas nears an end, analysts from broker Everbright Futures said in a note

New-car registrations, a proxy for sales, in the European Union, Britain and the European Free Trade Association rose 3.4% year-on-year to 1.13 million vehicles in October, the European Automobile Manufacturers' Association said on Tuesday
Automobile sales could influence the intensity of automobile manufacturing, which involves using rubber-made tyres
Crude oil prices fell on Wednesday, paring some of the previous day's gains, as concerns over supply disruptions in the Middle East were offset by rising supply and the prospect of a market surplus
Natural rubber often takes direction from oil prices as it competes for market share with synthetic rubber, which is made from crude oil
Japan's Nikkei share average fell on Wednesday, as technology stocks tracked US peers' overnight declines, with chip-related Advantest and Tokyo Electron leading the declines
Weaker risk sentiment tends to weigh on rubber futures
The front-month rubber contract on Singapore Exchange's SICOM platform for February delivery (STFG7) last traded at 236.2 US cents per kg, up 0.1%

title: Japan futures edge up on tight supply, weaker oil and equities cap gains
